description: Manual Gold-contract reviews keyed by protocol slug. Candidate selection alone never implies Gold readiness.

active-recall-test-yourself.user_problem: I keep rereading material until it feels familiar, but I need to know whether I can actually retrieve it later and, when relevant, apply it.
eligibility: The target includes information, rules, concepts, vocabulary, or other material that the person needs to retrieve from memory.
The learner can compare the attempted answer with a trustworthy source or worked answer soon after retrieval.
The task is low-risk enough that practice errors can be corrected before the knowledge is used in a consequential setting.
when_not_to_use: Do not use memory recall alone as a substitute for supervised practice, competency assessment, or expert review in safety-critical, clinical, legal, financial, or other consequential work.
Do not assume recall practice by itself trains application, procedural execution, fluent production, judgment, or transfer to a new problem.
Do not keep guessing from memory when the material has not first been learned well enough to provide a meaningful retrieval target; learn or clarify the source first.
active-recall-test-yourself.first_action: Choose three to five things you genuinely need to remember, close the source, and try to produce the first answer before looking.
steps: Define the real outcome: retention, application, or both. This determines whether retrieval is the whole practice target or only one layer.
Hide the source and retrieve the target information using a question, cue, blank page, flashcard prompt, or short explanation.
Check the attempted answer against the source and explicitly correct missing or wrong parts instead of rehearsing unresolved guesses.
If the real outcome requires performance, add a fresh application task such as solving, writing, speaking, calculating, classifying, or performing.
At a later normal study opportunity, retrieve the weak items again and separately check whether the application task is improving.

review_horizon.value: At the next normal study or review session
review_horizon.rationale: The evidence supports retrieval practice for retention but does not establish one universal session length or spacing schedule. A later ordinary study opportunity provides a useful check without inventing a magic timer.

active-recall-test-yourself.observable_signal: Whether the learner can produce the target information without looking, identify and correct misses, and—if application matters—complete a separate representative application task.
active-recall-test-yourself.stop_or_change_rule: Change the protocol if retrieval is becoming reliable but the real application outcome is not improving; add or replace practice with tasks that more closely match the required performance. Stop using a source or exercise if feedback is unreliable, the material is unsafe to practise independently, or repeated errors cannot be checked confidently.
active-recall-test-yourself.fallback: If unaided retrieval is too difficult to be useful, reduce the material, relearn one small chunk, use a stronger cue, then try retrieval again with immediate checking rather than repeating blind failure.

evidence_boundary.statement: Applied classroom research supports retrieval practice as a useful strategy for learning and retention. Brali keeps the claim outcome-specific: later remembering is not the same as later application, and the broad label testing effect can combine distinct direct and forward effects.

limitations: The main supporting systematic review concerns school and classroom learning and is geographically concentrated in the United States and Western Europe.
The 2026 procedural classroom study concerns Dutch verb-spelling rules in fourth-grade pupils and should not be generalized into a universal claim about every complex skill.
The 2026 testing-effect meta-analysis narrows terminology and outcome interpretation; it does not establish one optimal retrieval format, timer, repetition count, or schedule.
Retrieval success for an individual item does not guarantee comprehension, transfer, judgment quality, motivation, or durable real-world performance.

source_citations: Agarwal PK, Nunes LD, Blunt JR. Retrieval Practice Consistently Benefits Student Learning: a Systematic Review of Applied Research in Schools and Classrooms. Educational Psychology Review. 2021. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10648-021-09595-9

Research on the testing effect routinely conflates direct and forward testing effects: A meta-analysis of testing effects with free recall. Journal of Experimental Psychology: Learning, Memory, and Cognition. 2026. https://doi.org/10.1037/xlm0001634

Ophuis-Cox FHA, Catrysse L, Camp G. Mixed effects of retrieval practice on the acquisition of procedural knowledge in verb spelling education. Learning and Instruction. 2026. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.learninstruc.2026.102377

active-recall-test-yourself.agent_summary: Use this protocol when the user needs to retain learned material. Ask them to retrieve before looking, check and correct errors, and add a separate representative application task whenever success means doing rather than merely remembering. Do not invent a universal timer or imply that recall automatically transfers to skill.
